# onpager_rbac_permissions (Data Source)

Read the complete native permission catalog as public metadata. Reading the catalog grants no permissions and does not describe any principal's effective access.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onpager_rbac_permissions" "example" {}

output "teams_read_metadata" {
  value = data.onpager_rbac_permissions.example.permissions["teams.read"]
}

output "teams_read_supports_service_accounts" {
  value = contains(
    data.onpager_rbac_permissions.example.permissions["teams.read"].actors,
    "service_account",
  )
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Literal catalog identity: `catalog`. This data source has no selectors.
- `permissions` (Attributes Map) Complete catalog keyed by each exact native permission key. An empty API array produces an empty map. Future permission keys and sections are preserved without a provider allowlist. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--permissions))

<a id="nestedatt--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `permissions`

Read-Only:

- `actors` (Set of String) Compatible actor kinds: `user` and/or `service_account`. Absence of `service_account` identifies a permission unavailable to machine roles.
- `custom_grantable` (Boolean) Whether the API permits this permission in a custom role, subject to its scope and actor constraints. A true value grants no authority.
- `description` (String) API permission description; an empty string is preserved.
- `name` (String) API permission name.
- `scopes` (Set of String) Compatible role scopes: `tenant` and/or `team`. This metadata assigns no scope or grant.
- `section` (String) API catalog section, including sections introduced by later catalog releases.
- `sensitive` (Boolean) Public metadata flag identifying a sensitive action. This boolean is not a secret and is not marked sensitive in Terraform.
- `target` (String) Authorization target kind: `tenant`, `team` or `self`.

## Read behavior

This data source has no arguments or selectors. It reads the complete
unpaginated catalog through one authenticated `GET /v1/rbac/permissions` and
returns a map keyed by each exact native permission key. The computed `id` is
the literal `catalog`. An empty API array produces an empty map. Permission
keys and section names introduced by the API are preserved without a provider
allowlist. Denied access, malformed or incomplete metadata, duplicate permission
keys and transport failures produce diagnostics.

The catalog describes available permissions. It does not describe the caller's
or another principal's effective access, assign roles, create grants or call an
access explanation endpoint. Select desired permission keys explicitly when
configuring a custom role; catalog membership alone is not authority.

`actors` identifies compatible actor kinds. A permission whose actor set lacks
`service_account` cannot be used by a service account. `scopes` and
`custom_grantable` describe further role constraints; the API remains the
authority when validating role changes. The `sensitive` boolean is public action
metadata and contains no credential or secret value.

## Permissions

Requires a valid personal bearer token or service account bearer token. Catalog
introspection requires no business grant such as `roles.read` and grants no
business access. Reads never modify configuration.
